chunks: Some of our companions, from Ibn Jamhūr, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, all together from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib will be resurrected as a community by himself. Upon him will be the splendor of kings and the mark of the Prophets, and that is because he was the first to speak of al-badāʾ.

He said: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had sent the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to his shepherds regarding camels of his that had strayed away. So he gathered them, but was delayed from returning to him. Then he took hold of the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah and began saying: “O Lord, will You destroy Your sign? If You do, then it is a matter that has appeared to You.”

Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came with the camels, while ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib had sent people in every road and every mountain pass searching for him, and he kept crying out: “O Lord, will You destroy Your sign? If You do, then it is a matter that has appeared to You.” When he saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, he took him and kissed him, and said: “O my son, after this I will not send you for anything, for I fear that you may be treacherously attacked and killed.”

key_terms.أُمَّةً: a community; here, one person counted with the rank of a whole community
key_terms.الْبَدَاءِ: al-badāʾ; the manifestation of a matter in divine decree
key_terms.تُغْتَالَ: to be treacherously attacked or assassinated
key_terms.حَلْقَةِ بَابِ الْكَعْبَةِ: the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah
key_terms.سِيمَاءُ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the distinguishing mark or appearance of the Prophets
key_terms.يُبْعَثُ: will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s belief in al-badāʾ and his status on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the lofty rank of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and states that he will be resurrected as a community by himself. It also relates an incident from the childhood of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله that illustrates ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s deep concern for him and explicitly connects his words to belief in al-badāʾ.

en.hubeali:

Will You<sup>azwj</sup> Destroy Your Sign? If You<sup>azwj</sup> do so, it would be a matter what is Changed for You<sup>azwj</sup>’.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> came over with the camels, and Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup> had looked for him<sup>saww</sup> in every road and in every cave seeking him<sup>saww</sup>, and went on shouting: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! When he<sup>as</sup> saw Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, he<sup>as</sup> grabbed him<sup>saww</sup>, and kissed him<sup>as</sup>, and said: ‘O my<sup>as</sup> son<sup>saww</sup>! I<sup>as</sup> will not divert you<sup>saww</sup> after this with regards to anything, for I<sup>as</sup><sup>ws</sup> fear that you<sup>saww</sup> might be assassinated, murdered’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-’Asamm from al-Hatham ibn Waqid from Muqarrin from abu ‘‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“ ‘Abd al-Muttalib is the first one who believer in Bada’ (Allah’s revised will). He will be resurrected as a whole nation. He will have a august presence like kings and an countenance like the prophets.”
